What did the Tribunals Reforms Act do?

claims.claim: L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (18 March 1997), seven-judge bench: judicial review under Articles 226 and 32 is part of the basic structure; tribunal decisions are subject to High Court review under Articles 226/227
The April 2021 Ordinance set a four-year term and a minimum age of 50; the Supreme Court struck these down in July 2021

The Tribunals Reforms Act 2021 retained the four-year term and minimum age of 50, and abolished several appellate bodies (e.g. under the Cinematograph Act and Patents Act), transferring their functions mainly to High Courts
On 19 November 2025 the Supreme Court struck down the Act's minimum age of 50 and four-year tenure, saying the Centre had revived provisions earlier declared unconstitutional
The Court directed the Union to set up a National Tribunals Commission within four (4) months

review_note: L. Chandra Kumar facts from the official judgment PDF (digiscr.sci.gov.in).
